adversarial_critique: Claude's headline estimate (+0.059**, SE = 0.027, p < 0.05, N = 3,182) and Favourable direction accurately reflect the primary modified difference-in-differences result for improved water source access in Table 5, Column (3) (PDF p. 9), which is qualitatively and quantitatively confirmed by propensity-score-matched DD (Section 5(c), PDF pp. 8-9) and reinforced by an unextracted co-primary WASH finding of +0.151*** (SE = 0.0347, p < 0.01) for toilet/sanitation access in Table 5, Column (4). However, Claude's comparator_full contains a design misdescription: it states that households in PETT areas are 'compared across pre/post program-rollout timing,' whereas Section 5(b) (PDF p. 8) explicitly relies on a single 2004 cross-sectional survey and identifies off spatial rollout (program vs. non-program villages) interacted with pre-PETT title status (no prior title vs. prior non-PETT title). Across secondary water outcomes and mechanism models, effects are weaker or null: river-water reliance falls only at the 10% level (-0.043*, SE = 0.024, Table 5 Col 2), tanker/vendor use is null (0.005, SE = 0.009, Table 5 Col 1), realizing a public water network connection in the prior 5 years is borderline at 10% (0.032*, SE = 0.019, Table 6 Panel A Col 1, PDF p. 10), and household out-of-pocket water spending, credit use, and monthly water payments are all null (Table 6 Panel A Cols 2-4; PDF pp. 10-11). An additional technical trap in the Elsevier PDF text layer is that Unicode minus glyphs are stripped from negative coefficients in Tables 4-7 (e.g., Table 5 Col 2 prints -0.043* as 0.043* and Table 7 Cols 5-6 print -0.110*** and -0.067** without minus signs), though the prose on PDF pp. 1, 9, and 11 unambiguously confirms that improved water source (+0.059**) is positive and river-water and unmet-need effects are negative. Because both primary causal WASH access outcomes (improved water and sanitation) are statistically significant at conventional levels in the favourable direction and directly test formal rural land titling (Family A), the stored directional coding is fully supported.

numerical_check_note: Exact match to Table 5, Column (3) on PDF p. 9: the modified DD interaction term (program * no prior) for 'Improved source' is 0.059** with standard error (0.027), significant at the 5% level (** p < 0.05), on N = 3,182 household observations (total survey sample N = 3,204 in Tables 1-3; omitted untitled mean = 0.766 in Table 4, PDF p. 7). Expressing the linear probability model coefficient 0.059 as +5.9 pp in estimate_short is exact, though comparator_full inaccurately refers to pre/post longitudinal comparison rather than the cross-sectional spatial-by-prior-title double difference in Eq. (1) (PDF p. 8).
polarity_or_orientation_issue: None for the extracted estimate: 'Improved water source' is coded higher = better (binary = 1 for indoor tap, outdoor tap, fountain, or well/spring) and exposure (program * no prior = 1) represents formal rural land-title eligibility under PETT, so raw sign '+' cleanly maps to Favourable. Note a PDF text-layer pitfall on secondary reverse-polarity outcomes: Elsevier's text layer omits minus signs in Tables 4-7 (e.g., River in Table 5 Col 2 prints as 0.043* rather than -0.043*, and unmet community network need in Table 7 Cols 5-6 prints as 0.110*** and 0.067** rather than -0.110*** and -0.067**), but prose on PDF pp. 9 and 11 confirms their true negative signs.
